governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

findings.description: The file-backed command queue is asynchronous, so writing the marker before returning a snapshot does not prove the runtime observed it before an already-due watchdog check kills the session.
findings.recommendation: Require an acknowledgment or equivalent atomic coordination before returning success, and test attachment racing an idle or completion deadline.

result.summary: Require a successful Toolbar attachment to win atomically against timeout enforcement.

checklist.description: Extend the Goal Agent session control contract with an exact-session Toolbar attachment request carrying a unique acknowledgment identity and a persisted one-way protected state, while keeping ordinary input, resize, and non-Toolbar attachment semantics unchanged.

Coordinate attachment inside the Goal Agent runtime so it records the protected state and matching acknowledgment before evaluating either watchdog, making every acknowledged attachment win against an idle or completion deadline.

Make the Toolbar Goal Agent route wait for and validate the matching acknowledgment from the same still-live session before returning its snapshot, and return a conflict or unavailable result if the session exits or the acknowledgment cannot be established.

Once protected, bypass only idle and completion timeout termination while preserving valid completion-signal settlement, needs-input behavior, explicit Stop and Goal cancellation, natural process exit, transcript capture, and workflow ownership.

Add focused regressions for unattached timeout enforcement, acknowledged survival beyond both watchdogs, exact-session and non-Toolbar isolation, deadline races, failed attachment without false success, and later completion or explicit termination.
Update the Goal Agent and Toolbar intent pages to describe acknowledged Toolbar attachment, the automatic-timeout exemption, and the unchanged explicit and workflow-owned lifecycle boundaries.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: The runtime processes an attachment request by persisting a protected state and its unique acknowledgment before either watchdog check, and the Toolbar route returns success only after it observes that acknowledgment for the exact live session; deadline-race coverage proves an acknowledged open cannot be followed by timeout termination while a losing race cannot be reported as a successful attachment.

result.summary: Make opening a live workflow Goal Agent from the Toolbar a one-way, runtime-acknowledged attachment that disables its idle and completion watchdogs before the open succeeds, so a session the user has actually opened cannot be killed by an automatic timeout while unattended sessions remain bounded.

governance_precheck.message: The finalized plan does not require violating any governance rule or enabled guidance.

checklist.evidence: Added the ToolbarAttach session command with a per-request UUID acknowledgment, persisted toolbar_timeout_protected state and acknowledgment identities in the exact managed process record, and exposed the protected state in session snapshots while leaving Input, Resize, and non-Toolbar routes unchanged.

The Goal Agent runtime consumes ToolbarAttach commands at the top of its poll loop and registers the protected flag plus matching acknowledgment in one process-record update before inspecting exit/signals or evaluating either watchdog.

The Toolbar Goal route now waits for the requested acknowledgment on the same process id and session id, rechecks liveness before returning the snapshot, returns conflict for an exited or changed session, and returns degraded/unavailable when acknowledgment is not established.

Only completion-timeout and idle-timeout verdicts are gated by the one-way protected state. Existing signal processing, needs-input attention, process exit, transcript capture, process-group cleanup, workflow settlement, cancellation, and Stop paths remain authoritative; regressions prove later valid completion and workflow-aware Stop still settle.

Added focused attachment tests for near-deadline acknowledgment winning before both watchdogs, survival after both deadlines, unique repeated acknowledgments, exact-session and non-Goal isolation, missing acknowledgment without false success, and later valid completion. Existing unattached hard-cap/idle tests remain green, and web lifecycle coverage verifies acknowledged open plus explicit Stop.

Updated docs/intent Goal Agents and Toolbar pages with exact-session acknowledged attachment, the automatic-timeout exemption, fail-closed open races, and unchanged explicit/workflow lifecycle boundaries.

implementation.report: Implemented runtime-acknowledged Toolbar attachment for workflow Goal Agents. Toolbar opens now request a unique exact-session acknowledgment, wait for the same live process to persist one-way timeout protection, and fail closed on exit, mismatch, or missing acknowledgment. The runtime processes and persists attachment before watchdog evaluation, bypasses only idle and completion timeouts after protection, and preserves valid completion, needs-input, explicit Stop/cancellation, natural exit, transcript, worktree, and workflow settlement behavior. Updated Goal Agent and Toolbar intent documentation and added focused runtime and HTTP regressions. Verification: formatting, 34 Goal Agent session tests, 10 Goal lifecycle tests, 37 Toolbar browser tests, and changed-code Clippy passed. The 1,102-test library run had one unrelated source-promotion timing failure (1095 passed, 1 failed, 6 ignored); that exact untouched test passed on immediate isolated rerun.

checklist.description: Extend the Goal Agent session command and process metadata contract with a one-way Toolbar attachment marker that can be applied to the exact live session without creating a duplicate agent.
Have the Toolbar terminal-session route mark an existing Goal Agent as attached before returning its snapshot while preserving the default and CLI attachment behavior without the exemption.

Change the Goal Agent runtime to stop enforcing idle and completion timeout termination after the attachment marker is observed while retaining completion-signal handling, needs-input behavior, explicit Stop or cancellation, natural exit, transcript capture, and workflow settlement.

Add focused session and web-route regression coverage for unattached timeout enforcement, attached survival beyond both deadlines, exact-session marking, and later clean completion or explicit termination.

Update the affected Goal Agent and Toolbar intent pages to document that opening the workflow-owned session disables automatic timeout termination without changing its workflow ownership or explicit lifecycle controls.

result.summary: Mark a live workflow Goal Agent as user-attached when it is opened from the Toolbar and exempt that session from idle and completion timeouts so the user's terminal is not killed while unattended agents remain bounded.
